title: Deploying YOLO for whole-slide mitosis detection: A transparent, auditable, and reproducible pipeline for pathology AI-assisted diagnosis and decision-support tool

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Deploying YOLO for whole-slide mitosis detection: A transparent, auditable, and reproducible pipeline for pathology AI-assisted diagnosis and decision-support tool》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction/Background · p0010】Mitotic figure detection is a crucial component in evaluating tumor proliferation, and histopathology is still the gold-standard for cancer diagnosis and grading.1 Reproducible grading requires accurate mitosis identification, but manual counting takes time and is prone to inter-observer variability.2 This procedure has been automated by artificial intelligence (AI) systems; nevertheless, a large number of commercial AI solutions are opaque, costly, and proprietary. High license fees prevent use in diagnostic labs with limited resources, and its “black box” nature restricts openness.3

【Introduction/Background · p0015】The Royal College of Pathologists (RCPath), which oversees clinical practice in the UK, places a strong emphasis on auditability, repeatability, and transparency in diagnostic workflows.4 AI systems must produce interpretable results and keep audit trails that regulators and physicians may examine in order to be trusted in pathology.2 Every inference run generates structured logs, CSV outputs, heatmaps, and per-tile debug overlays, guaranteeing that detections can be tracked, validated, and audited. Our pipeline is specifically built with RCPath compliance in mind. This strategy encourages confidence among pathologists who need visibility into choices in addition to supporting clinical governance.5

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Deploying YOLO for whole-slide mitosis detection: A transparent, auditable, and reproducible pipeline for pathology AI-assisted diagnosis and decision-support tool》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · p0030】AI models are strengthened and empowered in the crucible of training and benchmarking. In order to provide predictions, the model learns to identify patterns through computer vision. These training data offer the chance to test performance against established datasets and are primarily of historical origin.6 Patch-level benchmarking, model and inference pipeline design, training settings, entire slide inference pipeline, output/result considerations, and pathologist expert validation will all be covered in this part.

【Methods · abstract-2-1】We developed a transparent and repeatable process for mitosis identification using YOLOv8, designed to scale from full slide inference to patch-level benchmarking. Global non-maximum suppression (NMS), GPU accelerated inference, region of interest-driven and adaptive tiling, and tissue gating are all integrated into the pipeline. In order to facilitate expert validation and traceability, audit-ready outputs include detection CSVs, tile manifests, positive and negative overlays, and heatmaps.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Deploying YOLO for whole-slide mitosis detection: A transparent, auditable, and reproducible pipeline for pathology AI-assisted diagnosis and decision-support tool》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Expert review validation · p0110】Two pathology specialists were asked to examine representative tile-level overlays detected by the pipeline in order to evaluate the clinical significance of the model outputs. Two (2) consultant histopathologists with over 10 years of histopathology experience were among the reviewers.

【Expert review validation · p0115】Each reviewer independently evaluated:•The proportion of detections corresponding to true mitotic figures.•The presence and nature of FPs and FNs.•Whether the model-identified hotspots aligned with diagnostically relevant regions.•Clarity and interpretability of the visual outputs.•Perceived usefulness as a screening or decision-support tool.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Deploying YOLO for whole-slide mitosis detection: A transparent, auditable, and reproducible pipeline for pathology AI-assisted diagnosis and decision-support tool》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · f0005】Fig. 1 Graphical abstract of process overview of the reproducible YOLOv8 pipeline for mitosis detection. After YOLOv8 processing and global non-maximum suppression, entire slide images are tiled into overlapping patches. Transparency and expert validation are made possible by outputs such as heatmaps, overlays, and CSV detections. The pipeline lays the foundation for integration into pathological workflows and clinical use.

【Fig. 2 · f0010】Fig. 2 Model accuracy across epochs demonstrates fast model learning and high validation performance in the training session.

【Fig. 3 · f0015】Fig. 3 Workflow diagram for whole-slide images (WSIs) in the pipeline for mitotic detection. There are four steps in the pipeline: (1) Tile extraction: the WSI is separated into 512 × 512 pixel patches that overlap; (2) YOLO inference, in which a YOLOv8 model trained on mitosis patches processes each tile; (3) global non-maximum suppression, which eliminates duplicate detections across overlapping tiles, leaving only the highest confidence bounding boxes; and (4) output generation, which creates structured artifacts such as CSV detections, heatmap overlays, and per-tile debug images for expert review and auditability.
